title: The Postcard of Sandpiper Point
premise: Paloma Delacroix, a marine biologist hiding from a career-destroying scandal, takes a seasonal post at the Sandpiper Point sea turtle sanctuary, where she finds a decades-old postcard addressed to a woman who vanished from the town under mysterious circumstances. Her search for the postcard's story entangles her with Eli Navarro, the rival scientist whose testimony once ended her old career—and the man she loved and left in their twenties. As a storm season threatens both the nesting beach and the sanctuary's survival, Paloma must decide whether to expose the truth of her past to save the turtles, and whether to trust Eli, who has quietly spent years trying to find her. She chooses both: testifying to clear her name at the cost of the prestigious post she fled toward, and staying at Sandpiper Point, where the postcard's lost woman is found alive and Paloma finally claims the belonging she never believed she deserved.
about_author: Ines Montrose is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where everyone knows your business before you do. She lives within earshot of the Atlantic and swears the best romances begin with bad weather.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles, Not Heartbreaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Arriving at Sandpiper Point under a false sense of anonymity, she takes the sanctuary job after a scandal she refuses to name. She finds a water-stained 1978 postcard in the boathouse addressed to a woman named Ruth who 'left without goodbye.' Emotional beat: guarded relief curdling into curiosity—the past has followed her here.

chapters.title: The Man in the Rain Jacket
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The new visiting researcher turns out to be Eli Navarro, the rival whose data testimony ended her old career—and her heart—ten years ago. Their first survey together is all clipped professionalism and old wounds. Emotional beat: humiliation and anger, undercut by the unwelcome jolt of still knowing how he takes his coffee.

chapters.title: What Ruth Left Behind
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a letter from Ruth interleaved. Chasing the postcard, Paloma befriends Marisol, the sanctuary's octogenarian cook, who goes silent at Ruth's name. Meanwhile Eli proves unexpectedly gentle with a stranded hatchling. Emotional beat: the first crack in Paloma's armor—she wants to be seen, and hates that he's the one seeing.

chapters.title: Nesting Season, Nesting Secrets
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. He reveals he requested this posting deliberately; he's spent a decade trying to find her and to retract the flawed data he was pressured to confirm. Paloma slams the door on his apology. Emotional beat: his guilt and longing against her terror of trusting the man who broke her.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A nor'easter is forecast to hit during peak nesting, and the sanctuary's funding board threatens to pull out unless the season's numbers hold. Paloma and Eli must work through the night sandbagging nests, and old intimacy resurfaces in the dark. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership becoming something warmer and more dangerous.

chapters.title: Snowed In at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Stranded together when the road floods, they finally speak the truth of their twenties: she left because she was offered everything and believed love would cost her the career; he let her go because he thought she'd chosen ambition over him. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness colliding—'the best mistake of our lives.'

chapters.title: Marisol's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Marisol confesses Ruth was her sister, driven out by a scandal she didn't commit—the same pattern Paloma now lives. The parallel lands hard: staying invisible is a slow exile. Emotional beat: recognition and resolve; Paloma realizes her silence protects no one.

chapters.title: The Choice on the Table
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The board offers Paloma the permanent directorship—conditional on her keeping her past buried. Eli, meanwhile, is offered a prestigious post abroad, the career he sacrificed for her once already. Emotional beat: the trap closes; every option costs something she loves.

chapters.title: Testimony at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, climax. At the board hearing, Paloma tells the whole truth—her scandal, Eli's coercion by his old mentor, the falsified data—and forfeits the directorship. Eli, in turn, declines the post abroad. Emotional beat: terror turning to liberation as she chooses integrity over invisibility, and him over safety.

chapters.title: Where the Sandpipers Land
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, resolution. Months later: the sanctuary survives on community support, Ruth is found alive in a coastal town two states away and reunited with Marisol, and Paloma and Eli co-lead the station together. On the beach at dawn, the first hatchlings race for the sea. Emotional beat: belonging, earned at last—home was never a place she fled to, but a family she built.
